checked_claims: Claim A (reduction range) - CORRECT, sloppily written. SRC-0002 sec 6.2 gives H^BM_k(M_{g,n})=0 for k<2g when n=0,1 and k<2g-2+n when n>=2. For k=16, n>=2: n <= 18-2g, so n<=12 at g=3. The attempt's displayed derivation contains a garbled fragment ('n <= 2g+14-12 wait: n <= 16-2g+2') but 16-2g+2 = 18-2g = 12 is right. The 'n>=2' hypothesis silently dodges the different n=0,1 threshold (2g, not 2g-2+n) rather than stating it. Equation (6.1) is quoted correctly in its HOMOLOGICAL form (H_k(dhat Mbar) -> H_k(Mbar) -> W_{-k}H^BM_k(M) -> 0, SRC-0002 line 1219); no spurious Gysin shift was introduced (contrast the cohomological version with the -2 shift used in SRC-0002 for Thm 1.9).

Claim B (c(3)=11) - CORRECT. SRC-0002 Table 1 reads c(g) = inf,10,10,11,11,7,5,3 for g=0..7; SRC-0004 Cor. 7.5 gives A*(M_{3,n})=R*(M_{3,n}) and CKgP for n<=11. Cross-check of RED-0001's residual list against n<=18-2g and Table 1: g=3 needs n<=12 (c=11, gap at 12); g=4 needs n<=10 (c=11, covered - correctly absent from the list); g=5 needs n<=8 (c=7, gap); g=6 needs n<=6 (c=5, gap); g=7 needs n<=4 (c=3, gap); g=8 needs n<=2 via k>=2g for n=0,1 and k>=2g-2+n for n=2 (gap); g=9 excluded since 2g=18>16. No stable pair is omitted from RED-0001, and g<=2 is legitimately handled by other means in SRC-0002 (Cor. 2.7 for g=2), so the M_{2,11..14} pairs are not counterexamples. CONFIRMED.

Claim C (what CKgP buys) - PARTLY MIS-STATED. SRC-0002 Lemma 4.3 is correctly reported (X open in smooth proper DM Xbar with CKgP => cl: (+)A^i(X) -> (+)W_kH^k(X) surjective, hence W_kH^k pure Hodge-Tate for even k). But Prop. 4.5 is NOT 'the same input': it concludes W_kH^k = RH^k and needs A*(M_{g,n}) = R*(M_{g,n}) in addition to CKgP. Since Claim N(ii) explicitly disclaims A*=R* for M_{3,12}, the attempt is not entitled to Prop. 4.5's tautological conclusion, only to Lemma 4.3's algebraicity. GAP-3 concedes this, but Claim C states Prop. 4.5 as 'exactly what the low-homology induction uses,' which is the tautological-generation upgrade the adversary brief flags. Non-fatal for a pure-Tate-only target, but the two must not be quoted interchangeably.

Claim D (excision into Hyp + plane quartics) - CORRECT. Matches SRC-0004 Cor. 7.5 verbatim in structure: Hyp_{3,n} closed, M_{3,n} minus Hyp_{3,n} = F_{4,n}, and G_{d,n} -> F_{d,n} a mu_3-banded gerbe with A*(F) = A*(G) and CKgP equivalence (SRC-0004 line 1229 and Lemma 3.6). The mu_3-gerbe step genuinely requires Q-coefficients; the attempt flags this (Assumption 1) rather than smuggling it. Stack-vs-coarse is also clean (Assumption 2, and SRC-0004 Lemma 3.9 makes CKgP insensitive to the coarse space anyway, so no trap here).

Claim E (independent-conditions presentation) - CORRECT AS APPLIED, FALSE AS STATED. SRC-0004 Lemmas 7.1-7.2 and 7.4 are cited with the right ranges (n<=3d-1, and Lemma 7.4 additionally needs d>=4, using d-3 != 0). But the parenthetical 'evaluation of degree-d forms at the n points is surjective on that range' is false without Lemma 7.1's hypothesis that the points lie in the smooth locus of an irreducible nodal degree-d plane curve: 11 collinear points impose only 5 conditions on quartics (such quartics contain the line, so the kernel has dim h^0(O(3))=10). Harmless because the attempt only ever applies it to points on the quartic itself.

Claim F (sharpness of n<=11) - CORRECT. Exactly reproduces SRC-0004 line 1273: deg(O_{P^2}(-d)|_C tensor omega_C(Gamma)) = -d^2 + 2g-2 + n = -3d+n, which is n-12 at d=4. Independently re-derived: deg O(-4)|_C = -16, deg omega_C = 4.

Claim G (Hyp_{3,12}) - CORRECT, and better supported than the attempt says. SRC-0004 Thm 6.1 alone gives only A*(Hyp_{g,n}) generated by psi classes for n<=2g+6, NOT CKgP; CKgP comes from Thm 6.2 (I_{g,n} has CKgP for n<=2g+6) plus Lemma 3.3, since Hyp_{3,12} is open in I_{3,12}. This is exactly the route SRC-0004 uses in the proof of Cor. 7.5 ('Hyp_{3,n} has the CKgP, as discussed in Section 6'). At g=3, 2g+6 = 12, so n=12 is the last admissible value. CONFIRMED.

Claim H (stratify U_nh) - CORRECT and unproblematic. Lemma 7.2's tower G ==> PK_{d,n} -> U ==> (PV)^n -> BSL_3 is built over U := the open locus of (PV)^n where the evaluation (7.1) IS surjective, so the tower exists for every n; Lemma 7.1's only job is to guarantee that the image of G_{d,n} lands in U. Hence PK_{4,12}|_{U_ind} is still an open in a projective-bundle tower over BSL_3, G_ind is open in it, and N = image(G_ind) is a CKgP open in U_nh (D closed by semicontinuity). This step survives the n=12 wall intact.

Claim I (dependent locus) - CORRECT, and sharper than claimed. O_C(1) = omega_C on a smooth plane quartic, residual = O_C(Gamma-3) of degree 12-12 = 0, and surjectivity of Ev fails iff h^1(O_C(4)-Gamma) = h^0(O_C(Gamma-3)) != 0 iff O_C(Gamma) = O_C(3). This is an iff, not just one direction, so D is exactly the cubic-section locus. Dimension check: dim D = 6 (plane quartics mod PGL_3) + 9 (choice of cubic) = 15 = codim 3 in the 18-dimensional U_nh; equivalently 9 + 11 + 3 - 8 = 15 counting (Q, Gamma in |O_Q(4)|, C in the residual A^3).

Claim J (incidence presentation) - LOAD-BEARING AND UNPROVED. This is the strongest attack; see strongest_attack. The UNORDERED incidence locus is indeed open in P(Sym^4 V^dual) x_{BSL_3} P(Sym^3 V^dual) (dim 14+9-8 = 15, matching Claim I) and does have CKgP by SRC-0004 Lemmas 3.3 and 3.7. But D subset M_{3,12} carries LABELED markings, so D = I_ordered, a degree-12! finite etale ordering cover of that open. None of the cited results (SRC-0004 Lemmas 3.3, 3.7; SRC-0002 Prop. 4.2(1),(4),(5),(6)) yields CKgP for a finite etale cover of a CKgP base, and Prop. 4.2(2) / SRC-0004 Lemma 3.10 run in the opposite direction: a proper surjective representable I -> I_unordered transports CKgP DOWN from I, i.e. it would need what is to be proved as its input. Claim J's 'hence I has CKgP' is therefore unsupported.

Claim K (uniqueness of the cubic) - LINEAR ALGEBRA CORRECT, GAP MISPLACED. h^0(O_C(3)) = 12-3+1 = 10 with h^1 = h^0(O_C(-2)) = 0, and ker(H^0(O_{P^2}(3)) -> H^0(O_C(3))) = H^0(O_{P^2}(-1)) = 0, so the map is an isomorphism of 10-dimensional spaces and the cubic is unique up to scale. Moreover the properness worry of GAP-1 is largely self-solving: h^0(O_C(Gamma-3)) is identically 1 on D, so pi_*O_C(Gamma-3) is a line bundle on D and produces a canonical inverse D -> I by cohomology and base change. GAP-1 is thus the easy half of the problem, not the hard one.

Claim L (excision synthesis) - STRUCTURALLY VALID, ARITHMETICALLY UNDER-SPECIFIED. The excision architecture is legitimate: SRC-0004 Lemma 3.4 / SRC-0002 Prop. 4.2(3) do give CKgP from a finite stratification into CKgP strata, and neither requires smoothness of the closed stratum. But the conclusion is stated at the wrong cohomological degree. With d = dim M_{3,12} = 3g-3+n = 18, Poincare duality gives W_{-16}H^BM_16(M_{3,12}) = W_20 H^20(M_{3,12})(18), so what Lemma 4.3 must supply is surjectivity of A^10 onto W_20 H^20 (note 20 = vcd(M_{3,12}) = 4g-4+n, consistent with 16 = 2g-2+n being the bottom nonvanishing BM degree). The twist then lands correctly: Q(-10)(18) = Q(8), of weight -16, so 'a direct sum of Q(8)' is right. Degree 20 is never named anywhere in the attempt, and 'In particular' after 'W_kH^k' reads as if k=16 on both sides. This is saved only by Lemma 4.3 being stated for all k at once; a writeup that quoted it at k=16 alone would be simply wrong. GAP-4 admits the derivation is not done but does not record the numbers.

Claim M and Claim N (scope and disclaimers) - HONEST AND ACCURATE. RED-0001's five residual inputs are correctly enumerated (verified above), and one discharged case would not prove RED-0001. The declined shortcuts in Claim N(iii)/GAP-7 (Chenevier-Lannes conductor-1 predictions, Bergstrom-Faber point counts conditional on them, l-adic semisimplification, an unproved perfectness of an admcycles RH^8 x RH_8 pairing) are exactly the forbidden moves, and none is used anywhere in Claims A-L. No predicted motive is promoted to a theorem; no semisimplification is passed off as a Hodge-structure isomorphism (and the target W_{-16}H^BM_16 spanned by algebraic classes really is (+)Q(8) on the nose, since it is pure of weight -16 with all classes of type (-8,-8)).

GAP-2 - VACUOUS, and its vacuity discredits the gap inventory. The markings p_1..p_12 are pairwise disjoint sections, so Gamma is a reduced degree-12 divisor; since deg(C.Q) = 4*3 = 12 = deg Gamma, C.Q = Gamma as divisors, forcing C intersect Q to be reduced and transverse automatically (a shared tangent or flex would give multiplicity >= 2). Assumption 5 therefore restricts nothing. Likewise 'strata where Ev has corank >= 2' are empty: corank = h^0(O_C(Gamma-3)) <= 1 always, since a degree-0 line bundle on an irreducible curve has h^0 <= 1. Both halves of GAP-2 are non-problems.

strongest_attack: The single load-bearing new step, CKgP for the dependent locus D, is asserted in Claim J via lemmas that cannot reach it, and the failure is about ORDERED versus UNORDERED markings. D sits inside M_{3,12}, whose twelve markings are LABELED, so D = I_ordered. What is open in the projective-bundle product P(Sym^4 V^dual) x_{BSL_3} P(Sym^3 V^dual) is the unordered incidence locus of pairs (C,Q) (dimension 14+9-8 = 15, matching the independent count dim D = 6+9 = 15, codimension 3 in the 18-dimensional U_nh); the ordered stack is a degree-12! finite etale cover of it. CKgP does not ascend along finite etale covers, and every tool the attempt cites for this step points the wrong way: SRC-0002 Prop. 4.2(1) and SRC-0004 Lemma 3.3 apply only to OPEN substacks; Prop. 4.2(5)/Lemma 3.7 only to Grassmann bundles; and Prop. 4.2(2)/SRC-0004 Lemma 3.10 transport CKgP DOWNWARD along proper surjective representable maps, so applied to I -> I_unordered they consume exactly the statement to be proved. Prop. 4.2(3) does not help either, since it builds CKgP from strata rather than inheriting it. Nor is there an obvious repair: the natural ordered model over (PV)^12 requires the locus where twelve distinct points have corank exactly 1 on cubics, but twelve general points impose all 10 conditions, so that locus is LOCALLY CLOSED (generic corank 0) rather than open, and locally closed substacks of a CKgP stack need not have CKgP. Building it instead as {p_1..p_9 independent on cubics, then p_10,p_11,p_12 on the resulting unique cubic} stalls at the universal cubic curve, which is not a projective bundle over that base. This is precisely why n = 3d-1 = 11 is a real wall and not bookkeeping: the residual O_C(Gamma-3) of degree 0 makes the cubic-section locus an Abel-Jacobi fiber condition, not a projective-bundle degeneration. Aggravating the finding, this failure appears NOWHERE in GAP-1 through GAP-7: GAP-1 addresses properness of phi: I -> D, which is in fact nearly automatic (h^0(O_C(Gamma-3)) = 1 identically on D, so pi_*O_C(Gamma-3) is a line bundle giving a canonical inverse D -> I), and GAP-2 is outright vacuous (distinct markings force C.Q = Gamma reduced, hence transverse, and corank <= 1 everywhere since a degree-0 bundle on an irreducible curve has h^0 <= 1). So the attempt's declared gaps are the two easy points while the one genuinely unproved step is stated as established. Secondary attack, independent of the above: Claim L never names the cohomological degree it actually needs. With d = dim M_{3,12} = 18, Poincare duality gives W_{-16}H^BM_16(M_{3,12}) = W_20 H^20(M_{3,12})(18), so Lemma 4.3 must be invoked in degree 20 = vcd(M_{3,12}) = 4g-4+n and codimension 10, not 16 and 8. The Tate twist does land correctly (Q(-10)(18) = Q(8), weight -16, so the claimed sum of Q(8) is right), and the claim survives only because Lemma 4.3 is stated for all k simultaneously; GAP-4 concedes the derivation is missing but records none of these numbers. Verdict: incomplete, consistent with the attempt's own GAP-5, but incomplete for a reason the attempt has not identified.
